title: History of the Lovers of Syria

keywords: history of the lovers of syria
full_text:
In Damascus lived two noble families, the Banu Asad and the Banu Hilal, between whom an ancient rivalry had smoldered for generations over land boundaries and ancestral pride.

Yet fate decreed that young Walid of Banu Asad and gentle Salma of Banu Hilal should meet during a festival at the Great Umayyad Mosque. Their hearts recognized each other immediately: their love was pure, devoid of malice, and guided by deep virtue.

Knowing their fathers' entrenched enmity, Walid refused to enter into deceitful elopement. He said to Salma:
'Our love must heal our families, not tear them apart. I will win thy father's blessing through honor, or perish in the attempt.'

Soon after, a devastating desert locust swarm attacked the fertile Ghouta orchards of Damascus, followed by a band of desert raiders seeking to pillage the distressed farms.
The estate of Salma's father, Sheikh Hilal, was surrounded by raiders in the dead of night.

Walid, hearing the alarm bells, did not hesitate. Gathering his brothers and loyal kinsmen of Banu Asad, he rode into the fray, fighting courageously to break the siege. During the fierce combat, Walid threw himself before a falling blade meant for Sheikh Hilal, taking a severe wound to his shoulder to shield his father's rival.

The raiders were driven off. As Sheikh Hilal held the bleeding young hero in his arms, tears of shame and gratitude fell upon his beard.
'Young man,' cried the elder, 'thou hast shed thy blood to protect the man who hated thy father! Such nobility shames all ancient grudges!'

Walid's father, Sheikh Asad, arrived at dawn. Seeing his wounded son and his former rival embracing in mutual tears, the two patriarchs clasped hands over Walid's sickbed, renouncing their feud forever.

When Walid recovered, the entire city of Damascus attended the wedding of Walid and Salma. Their union united the two houses in perpetual peace, proving that true love has the power to extinguish ancient fires of hatred and plant gardens of lasting reconciliation.
moral: Sincere love accompanied by self-sacrifice and honor elevates human life above petty factional disputes.
